units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
What does this mean? Ottavio here and YOUR friend! And you, father, have forgotten my name. You are indeed turned to stone.
units.name: ANA

units.text: My dear: I am so much more admired in marble than I ever was in my own person that I have retained the shape the sculptor gave me. He was one of the first men of his day: you must acknowledge that.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: Father! Vanity! personal vanity! from you!
units.name: ANA

units.text: Ah, you outlived that weakness, my daughter: you must be nearly 80 by this time. I was cut off (by an accident) in my 64th year, and am considerably your junior in consequence. Besides, my child, in this place, what our libertine friend here would call the farce of parental wisdom is dropped. Regard me, I beg, as a fellow creature, not as a father.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: You speak as this villain speaks.
units.name: ANA

units.text: Juan is a sound thinker, Ana. A bad fencer, but a sound thinker.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: horror creeping upon her.
I begin to understand. These are devils, mocking me. I had better pray.
units.name: ANA

units.text: consoling her.

No, no, no, my child: do not pray. If you do, you will throw away the main advantage of this place. Written over the gate here are the words "Leave every hope behind, ye who enter." Only think what a relief that is! For what is hope? A form of moral responsibility. Here there is no hope, and consequently no duty, no work, nothing to be gained by praying, nothing to be lost by doing what you like. Hell, in short, is a place where you have nothing to do but amuse yourself.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: Don Juan sighs deeply.
You sigh, friend Juan; but if you dwelt in heaven, as I do, you would realize your advantages.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: You are in good spirits to-day, Commander. You are positively brilliant. What is the matter?
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: I have come to a momentous decision, my boy. But first, where is our friend the Devil? I must consult him in the matter. And Ana would like to make his acquaintance, no doubt.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: You are preparing some torment for me.
units.name: ANA

units.text: All that is superstition, Ana. Reassure yourself. Remember: the devil is not so black as he is painted.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Let us give him a call.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: At the wave of the statue's hand the great chords roll out again but this time Mozart's music gets grotesquely adulterated with Gounod's.
A scarlet halo begins to glow; and into it the Devil rises, very Mephistophelean, and not at all unlike Mendoza, though not so interesting.
He looks older; is getting prematurely bald; and, in spite of an effusion of goodnature and friendliness, is peevish and sensitive when his advances are not reciprocated.

He does not inspire much confidence in his powers of hard work or endurance, and is, on the whole, a disagreeably self-indulgent looking person; but he is clever and plausible, though perceptibly less well bred than the two other men, and enormously less vital than the woman.
heartily.
Have I the pleasure of again receiving a visit from the illustrious Commander of Calatrava?
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: Coldly.
Don Juan, your servant.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: Politely.
And a strange lady? My respects, Senora.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: Are you--
units.name: ANA

units.text: bowing.
Lucifer, at your service.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: I shall go mad.
units.name: ANA

units.text: gallantly.

Ah, Senora, do not be anxious. You come to us from earth, full of the prejudices and terrors of that priest-ridden place. You have heard me ill spoken of; and yet, believe me, I have hosts of friends there.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: Yes: you reign in their hearts.
units.name: ANA

units.text: shaking his head.

You flatter me, Senora; but you are mistaken. It is true that the world cannot get on without me; but it never gives me credit for that: in its heart it mistrusts and hates me. Its sympathies are all with misery, with poverty, with starvation of the body and of the heart. I call on it to sympathize with joy, with love, with happiness, with beauty.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: nauseated.
Excuse me: I am going. You know I cannot stand this.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: angrily.
Yes: I know that you are no friend of mine.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: What harm is he doing you, Juan? It seems to me that he was talking excellent sense when you interrupted him.
units.name: THE STATUE

units.text: warmly shaking the statue's hand.
Thank you, my friend: thank you. You have always understood me: he has always disparaged and avoided me.
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: I have treated you with perfect courtesy.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: Courtesy! What is courtesy? I care nothing for mere courtesy. Give me warmth of heart, true sincerity, the bond of sympathy with love and joy--
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: You are making me ill.
units.name: DON JUAN

units.text: There!
units.name: THE DEVIL

units.text: Appealing to the statue.
